explanation: Sewell wrote it to encourage kindness to working horses. Its title page called it the autobiography of a horse, 'translated from the original equine'.

claims.text: Black Beauty, published in 1877, was Anna Sewell's only novel.
The Black Stallion (Walter Farley), National Velvet (Enid Bagnold) and My Friend Flicka (Mary O'Hara) were written by other authors.
Black Beauty is narrated by the horse himself.
Sewell wrote Black Beauty to encourage the kind treatment of horses.
The original title page described the book as the autobiography of a horse 'translated from the original equine'.
